title: Pierce-bomb server-side parity — port the GDP-2026-05-26-002 blast-propagation branch into node-world-server
intent: S142 shipped Pierce-bomb on the client side. S142 notes explicitly defer the server-side parity: 'server-side blast-propagation in node-world-server gets the same branch in a follow-up story (deferred to a connected-mode sprint when one is open)'. This story IS that follow-up. Port the same single-block-pierce branch into the server's `BlastPropagationSystem`. After this lands, connected-mode players see Pierce work identically across tabs — without it, only solo mode honours pierce, and connected-mode pierce pickups become no-ops because the server still stops blasts at the first soft block.
rationale: Source: S142 sprint notes explicitly defer this work + GDP-2026-05-26-002 (the client-side pierce story). After multiplayer Sprint B (GDP-022-011, shipped S117-S125), the server is authoritative on blast propagation; any new client-side bomb behaviour that doesn't get a server twin becomes connected-mode-broken. Pierce is the first such gap. Marked `should` because connected mode keeps working for everything-but-pierce; solo players are unaffected. Small story — one branch in one server file + parity tests.
acceptanceHints: Depends on: GDP-2026-05-26-002 (client-side pierce) — SHIPPED S142. GDP-022-011 (server-authoritative gameplay) — SHIPPED S117-S125.

Reference: examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/blast-propagation-system.ts has the exact branch that lands here (single-block-pierce rule per direction). Mirror it 1:1 in the server-side equivalent — single source of truth would be ideal, but the existing client+server pattern uses code duplication (per S117-S125 architecture); the parity test asserts equivalence.
examples/backends/node-world-server: identify the kaboom-crew server-side blast-propagation module (whatever name it ended up with during the S117-S125 Sprint B port). Add the same branch:
Per direction from bomb origin: walk cells; stop at hard block; destroy + CONTINUE on first soft block IF Bomb.pierce; destroy + STOP on second soft block.
Each direction tracks its own pierce-budget (1) independently — identical to client.
PROTOCOL: protocol schema for the Bomb entity already includes the `pierce: boolean` field (shipped in S142 schema work). Server reads it from the placed Bomb component. No protocol changes needed.

BOMB PLACEMENT (server side): server's BombPlacementSystem must also copy BomberStats.pierce → Bomb.pierce at placement time (mirror of S142 FEAT-KABOOM-PIERCE-PLACEMENT-001). Verify this is already done — if it is (since the schema field exists), this story is just the propagation branch.
DETERMINISM: server's RNG-seeded pickup drops can still include pierce (drop table is per-cell deterministic). Same world seed → same pickup drops → same Pierce pickups available.
PARITY TEST (the key acceptance gate):
examples/backends/node-world-server/tests: add a parity test that runs the SAME blast scenario on client + server (in-process) and asserts identical BlastTile cell list. Test cases:
Pierce bomb at center of + of 2 soft blocks each direction → both blocks destroyed per direction, blast extends 1 cell past first block.
Pierce bomb at + of 3 soft blocks each direction → 2 destroyed per direction, third untouched.
Pierce bomb against mixed soft + hard → hard always stops, pierce credit irrelevant.
All three scenarios match between client + server.
ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST:

Two tabs join /?project=kaboom-crew&world=test&profile=connected. Tab A bomber picks up Pierce, places bomb adjacent to 2 soft blocks. Tab B's view shows the blast walking through both blocks (not stopping at the first). Round resolves identically on both tabs.
Before this story: Tab A's PIERCE LOOKS NORMAL on Tab A (client sim shows pierce), but Tab B sees the server-authoritative version which stops at first block — visual desync.
BOT AI: server-side bot AI sees Pierce in its action-scoring (same client-side ad-hoc treatment from S142 — bots collect but don't strategise). No new logic.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Pierce-aware bot AI improvements (carry-over from GDP-2026-05-26-002).
Stacking pierce (multi-block-pierce) — single-block remains the rule.
Network protocol changes (none required; existing snapshot carries pierce flag).
